Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We scoped internally and have three items we need clarified before procurement will greenlight the pilot: audit-log retention to 7 years, a KMS-backed HSM key for our EU PII-at-rest (we'll be US-based for processing but must coordinate cross-region key custody), and a HIPAA addendum with proof-of-evidence milestones.

Questions: 1) Can the audit log be exported daily to our S3? 2) How do you price the HSM seat vs per-token KMS use for mixed workloads? 3) Can you provide a phased billing plan so we can start with a pilot (3 months) and scale to a committed Dedicated pool?

We'd like a written outline (numbers) by EoD Monday if possible — procurement wants the chart for their Friday review next week.

Appreciate it,

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; Ben and Laura are looped for the pricing and implementation plan.

1) Audit logs: yes — daily export to your S3 is supported. We can offer two retention tiers: 1) managed retention on Redwood for 1/3/7 years; 2) delivery to your S3 with raw log files retained there (you control retention).

2) KMS/HSM: two pricing levers we typically use — an HSM seat (monthly, for on-prem or dedicated HSM instances) and a KMS per-call/throughput fee for hosted KMS usage. For hybrid custody (US processing with EU key custody) we recommend a single HSM-seat + per-call routing costs for cross-region requests. Ben will layout specific blended numbers.

3) Phased billing: we can structure pilot as a 3-month pilot with a one-time onboarding/assurance fee plus monthly pilot credits that convert to a committed discount if you commit to a 12‑month Dedicated pool within 60 days of pilot end. Laura will propose milestone-triggered credits tied to evidence delivery.

We'll attach a workbook with a few scenarios (pilot-only, pilot->dedicated commit, and direct dedicated) and an evidence timeline matrix. Will aim to get that to you Monday morning.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Sales, Compliance Solutions
Redwood Inference

Subject: RW-4821 — proposed fee table & concession mechanics (workbook attached)

Sarah — attaching the workbook we discussed. Highlights in plain language: 

- Pilot (3 months): one-time onboarding fee = $25k (covers initial HSM key setup, SOC-evidence packaging, and two security workshops). Monthly pilot fee = $6k (includes audit-log export + KMS calls at a capped throughput). Pilot credits = $15k applied at pilot close if you move to a 12‑month Dedicated commit.

- Dedicated commit (12 months): base dedicated fee = $12k/month for the reserved pool (baseline throughput), plus either: A) HSM-seat at $1,800/month (recommended for EU custody) or B) KMS per-100k-calls bucketed pricing at $0.65/1000 calls. We modeled mixed-workload costs in the workbook; the HSM-seat option amortizes better once sustained heavy crypto operations exceed ~50k keys/month.

- Audit-log retention options: Redwood-managed 7yr retention = $2,000/mo; S3-delivery + retention managed by Carely = one-time export automation setup $3,500 + no monthly Redwood retention fee.

- Evidence & milestones: we propose three deliverables tied to credits: (1) Audit log schema & export test (pilot month 1) — $5k credit; (2) HSM integration report (pilot month 2) — $5k credit; (3) Post-pilot compliance readiness sign-off (pilot month 3) — $5k credit (applied on invoice upon signing 12-month commitment).

See RW-4821-compliance-fee-workbench.xlsx (attached) for scenario rows. If you prefer a re-allocation of credits (e.g., larger onboarding fee reduction vs monthly credits) we can rework — quick calls usually fix this.

Next steps suggested: 1) confirm which custody model (HSM-seat vs KMS-buckets) you favor so we can lock the numbers; 2) sign addendum if you want the pilot reserved with the credits baked in (DocuSign link below); 3) schedule the initial security workshop the week pilot starts.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/RW-4821-addendum
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/54321RW-4821

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call to walk through the workbook.

Best,
Ben Carter
